objective.statement: Continue the independent CSV inspection sample by implementing repeatable --missing-value TOKEN options. Exact empty string is always missing; listed tokens add exact case-sensitive matches, with no trimming. Duplicate tokens never double-count. Default output and validation remain unchanged.
objective.done_when: Return implementable source and meaningful tests; the coordinator must execute them and record the result, not infer execution from your reply.
constraints: Public standard-library Python sample, not a new product or native Continuum feature.
The captured source contains README.md, inspect_csv.py, test_inspect_csv.py and sample.csv. Request the exact files needed before implementation; receiver has supplied text only, no filesystem tools.
Preserve quoted commas/newlines, unique nonempty headers, rectangular records, UTF-8 errors and no partial stdout on error.
Whitespace, case variants and padded tokens are present unless each is explicitly listed; --missing-value with an empty argument is valid and adds nothing beyond default.

decisions.statement: Use explicit opt-in exact missing tokens; do not infer common NA spellings or change output schema. Baseline four CLI integration tests passed in the coordinator environment; raw output is separate evidence, not authenticated by this authored decision.
decisions.reopen_when: An actual user requirement changes matching semantics.

uncertainties.question: Which source and test context does a fresh receiver need beyond this pack to implement the change correctly?
uncertainties.why_it_matters: The previous self-development pilot required extra source. This independent workload tests that boundary with different vocabulary.

handoff.scope: First request the necessary retained source files. After receiving them, implement the requirement and report needed/missing/unused context and extra retrieval. Do not claim execution.
